references.text: The prophet Isaiah uses the tree as a symbol of righteousness and blessing, similar to how good and bad trees are used in Matthew to represent righteous and wicked people.
The book of Psalms compares a righteous person to a tree planted by streams of water that bears fruit in its season, paralleling the idea of good trees bearing good fruit.
Jesus uses a similar image in Luke, stating that a tree is known by its fruit, which reflects the message in Matthew about good and bad trees.
Proverbs speaks of wisdom's fruit as a tree of life, which can be seen as related to the idea that good trees produce good fruit.
John's first letter discusses how children of God and children of the devil are made evident, which can be compared to the difference between good and bad trees in Matthew.
